group.passage: Imagine going to see a doctor and having him press his ear right against your chest. Before the stethoscope was invented, this was the usual way for a doctor to listen to a patient's heart and lungs. The method could embarrass both the patient and the doctor, and faint sounds were hard to hear. In 1816, a French doctor named René Laennec found a simple answer. That year, a young woman with signs of heart disease came to Laennec for help. Because of her age, her sex, and her size, he felt that putting his ear on her chest would not be proper. Then he thought of something he knew about sound: it travels well through solid things. If someone scratches one end of a long piece of wood with a pin, a person at the other end can hear it clearly. So Laennec rolled a sheet of paper into a tight tube, placed one end on the woman's chest, and put his ear to the other. Her heartbeat came through far more clearly than it ever had with his ear alone. Laennec, who played the flute in his free time, later replaced the paper with a better tool. He made a hollow wooden tube about 25 centimeters long. Because it was built in parts that could be taken apart, a doctor could easily carry it around. He called it the “stethoscope,” from two Greek words meaning “chest” and “to explore.” In 1819, he published a book explaining what the sounds of the heart and lungs could tell doctors about diseases. Not every doctor welcomed the stethoscope at first. Still, it soon spread. Doctors from all over Europe traveled to Paris to learn Laennec's method, and by the 1820s, stethoscopes could be found across Europe. Sadly, Laennec himself suffered from tuberculosis, a disease that most often attacks the lungs. He died in 1826, at the age of 45. Yet the simple tool that began as a roll of paper changed the way doctors examine their patients.

translation_zh.text:
想像一下，你去看醫生，醫生把耳朵直接貼在你的胸口上。在聽診器發明之前，這是醫生聽病人心臟和肺部的一般方法。這種方法可能讓病人和醫生都覺得尷尬，而且微弱的聲音很難聽清楚。1816 年，一位名叫雷奈克的法國醫生找到了一個簡單的解決辦法。
那一年，一位出現心臟病徵狀的年輕女子來找雷奈克看病。因為她的年齡、性別和體型，雷奈克覺得把耳朵貼在她胸口並不恰當。這時他想到自己知道的一個關於聲音的事實：聲音很容易經由固體傳過去。如果有人用針刮一根長木頭的一端，在另一端的人就能清楚聽到。於是雷奈克把一張紙緊緊捲成筒，一端放在那名女子的胸口，耳朵貼在另一端。她的心跳聲傳過來，比他以往只用耳朵聽時清楚得多。
雷奈克平時會吹長笛，他後來用一個更好的工具取代了紙筒。他做了一根約 25 公分長的中空木管。因為它是分成幾段做的、可以拆開，醫生可以很輕鬆地帶著走。他把它叫做「聽診器」（stethoscope），取自兩個希臘字，意思是「胸部」和「探查」。1819 年，他出版了一本書，說明心臟和肺部的聲音能告訴醫生哪些疾病的訊息。
起初並不是每個醫生都歡迎聽診器。不過，它很快就傳開了。歐洲各地的醫生前往巴黎學習雷奈克的方法，到了 1820 年代，歐洲各地都找得到聽診器。令人難過的是，雷奈克自己得了結核病，這是一種最常侵襲肺部的疾病。他在 1826 年去世，享年 45 歲。然而，這個從一卷紙開始的簡單工具，改變了醫生檢查病人的方式。
